html:
The Konomihu were a small people of the forks of the Salmon River in the mountains of northwestern California. Their language, now extinct, belonged to the Shastan family, and it was probably the most different member of that family. There may have been only a few speakers even before contact.

They fished salmon and gathered acorns among neighbours such as the Karuk and the New River Shasta. The Gold Rush brought miners up the Salmon River in the 1850s. By about 1900 the surviving Konomihu called themselves Shasta.
